concepts.name: Demand, composition and early working of the Constituent Assembly
concepts.description: From the idea of a Constituent Assembly to its composition under the Cabinet Mission Plan, its first meetings, the Objectives Resolution and the changes made by the Independence Act.
concepts.idea: The Assembly grew from a 1934 idea to a partly elected, partly nominated body of 389 that later became sovereign and a legislature.
concepts.rule: M.N. Roy put forward the idea in 1934, the Congress demanded it officially in 1935, Nehru gave the adult-franchise formulation in 1938, the August Offer of 1940 accepted it in principle and the Cabinet Mission rejected two Assemblies. The Assembly of 389 (292 + 93 + 4) was indirectly elected by communities (Muslims, Sikhs, General) through PR-STV, with state members nominated by rulers. It met first on 9 December 1946, Prasad became President on 11 December and Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December, adopted unanimously on 22 January 1947. The Independence Act made the Assembly sovereign and a legislature (Mavalankar presiding) and the strength fell to 299.
concepts.example: A statement that Prasad was elected at the first sitting on 9 December fails: the oldest member, Sinha, presided that day.

questions.q: The idea of a Constituent Assembly was first put forward in 1934 by M.N. Roy, a pioneer of the communist movement in India. In which year did the Indian National Congress officially demand a Constituent Assembly to frame the Constitution?
questions.e: Roy 1934, INC officially demanded the Assembly in 1935, Nehru's adult-franchise declaration in 1938, August Offer 1940, Cripps 1942.
w: 1938 is the year of Nehru's declaration on behalf of the Congress that the Assembly must be elected on adult franchise, not the first official demand.
1940 is the year of the August Offer, in which the British accepted the demand in principle.
1942 is the year of the Cripps proposals, which came from the British side.

questions.q: Out of the 296 seats allotted to British India in the Constituent Assembly under the Cabinet Mission scheme, the numbers drawn from the eleven Governors' Provinces and from the Chief Commissioners' Provinces respectively were
questions.e: : 292 members from eleven Governors' Provinces and 4 from the four Chief Commissioners' Provinces, one from each.
w: 289 and 7 would give the four Chief Commissioners' Provinces seven members, but each sent one.
293 and 3 would leave one of the four Chief Commissioners' Provinces without a member.
11 is the number of Governors' Provinces, not a number of seats; 285 and 11 confuses provinces with seats.

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly describes how the British Indian members of the Constituent Assembly were chosen under the Cabinet Mission scheme?
questions.a: Indirectly, by the members of each community in the provincial legislative assembly, through proportional representation by the single transferable vote
o: Indirectly, by the members of each community in the provincial legislative assembly, through proportional representation by the single transferable vote
Directly, by the adult voters of each province in territorial constituencies, through proportional representation by the single transferable vote
Indirectly, by the members of each community in the provincial legislative assembly, through the first-past-the-post method of voting
By nomination of the Governor of each province, in proportion to the strength of each community in the provincial legislative assembly, on the advice of party leaders
questions.e: Each community's members elected by that community's members in the Provincial Legislative Assembly, by PR-STV.
w: The members were not chosen by voters directly; the provincial assemblies, elected on a limited franchise, formed the electorate.
The method of voting was proportional representation by single transferable vote, not first-past-the-post.
Governors did not nominate British Indian members; only princely state members were nominated, and by their rulers.

questions.q: The freedoms of thought, expression, belief, faith, worship, vocation, association and action promised in the Objectives Resolution were to be enjoyed subject to
o: public order and the security of the State
the Directive Principles of State Policy
such restrictions as the Provisional Parliament may impose
questions.e: The freedoms were guaranteed 'subject to law and public morality'.
w: The Resolution did not mention public order or security of the State; its qualification was law and public morality.
Directive Principles were not mentioned as a limit on the freedoms in the Resolution.
The Resolution named no parliamentary power to restrict the freedoms; the qualification was law and public morality.

questions.q: The strength of the Constituent Assembly came down from the 389 fixed in 1946 to 299 mainly because
questions.a: the Muslim League members from the areas that went to Pakistan withdrew from it
o: the Muslim League members from the areas that went to Pakistan withdrew from it
the representatives of the princely states withdrew after the acceptance of the Mountbatten Plan
the Indian Independence Act abolished the seats of the Chief Commissioners' Provinces
a large number of Congress members resigned to contest the first general elections
questions.e: The strength fell to 299 as Muslim League members from the areas that went to Pakistan withdrew after Partition: the provinces' seats fell from 296 to 229 and the states' seats from 93 to 70.
w: After the Mountbatten Plan most princely state representatives took their seats in the Assembly rather than withdrawing.
The Act did not abolish the four Chief Commissioners' seats; the reduction followed the Partition.
Resignations of Congress members did not cause the fall; it followed the withdrawal of members from areas now in Pakistan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the road to the Constituent Assembly:

1. The British Government accepted the demand for a Constituent Assembly in principle through the August Offer of 1940.
2. The Cripps proposals of 1942 carried the idea of a body to frame India's Constitution.
3. The Cabinet Mission, consisting of Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander, rejected the demand for two separate Constituent Assemblies.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the August Offer of 1940 accepted it in principle. Statement 2 is correct: the 1942 Cripps Mission proposal included a constitution-making body. Statement 3 is correct: the Mission's members and its rejection of two Assemblies are stated on.
w: '2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the demand for a Constituent Assembly:

1. In 1938 Jawaharlal Nehru declared, for the Congress, that free India's Constitution must be framed without outside interference by an Assembly elected on adult franchise.
2. The British Government accepted the demand in principle through the Cripps Mission of 1942.
3. The Indian National Congress endorsed and reiterated Nehru's 1938 view by passing a resolution in 1939.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: in 1938 Nehru declared on behalf of the Congress that free India's Constitution must be framed without outside interference by an Assembly elected on adult franchise. Statement 2 is incorrect: the acceptance in principle came with the August Offer of 1940; the 1942 Cripps proposals only carried the idea of a constitution-making body. Statement 3 is correct: the Congress passed a resolution in 1939 endorsing and reiterating Nehru's view.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the seat allocation planned for the Assembly by the Cabinet Mission:

1. Of the 296 British Indian seats, 289 were to come from the eleven Governors' Provinces and 7 from the Chief Commissioners' Provinces.
2. The total strength was fixed at 389, of which 93 seats were allotted to the princely states.
3. Each of the four Chief Commissioners' Provinces was to send one member.
4. The yardstick for allotting seats to provinces and states was population, about one seat for each million people.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the split was 292 and 4. Statement 2 is correct: 389 in all, 296 for British India and 93 for the states. Statement 3 is correct: one member from each of the four provinces. Statement 4 is correct: population-based allocation, about one seat per million.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the choice of members of the Constituent Assembly:

1. Each British province's quota was split between three communities, Muslims, Sikhs and General, in proportion to their numbers.
2. The members from the princely states were elected by the people of those states.
3. Members of each community were elected by the members of that community in the provincial legislative assembly, through proportional representation by the single transferable vote.
4. The 93 seats allotted to the princely states stayed unfilled at first because the states decided to stay away from the Assembly.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: three communities: Muslims, Sikhs, General. Statement 2 is incorrect: they were nominated by the rulers of the princely states. Statement 3 is correct: indirect election by PR-STV. Statement 4 is correct: the 93 seats were not filled because the states stayed away.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

2. Dr Sachchidananda Sinha, the oldest member, was elected temporary President following French practice, and Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected President two days later.

Mukherjee was elected on 25 January 1947; V.T. Krishnamachari was elected second Vice-President on 16 July 1947. Statement 4 is correct: Rau was Constitutional Adviser.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements on how the Indian Independence Act, 1947 altered the position of the Constituent Assembly:

1. The Act confined the Assembly to framing the Constitution and took away its power to enact ordinary laws.
2. As a legislature, the Assembly sat under the chairmanship of Dr Rajendra Prasad.
3. After the Muslim League members from the areas now in Pakistan withdrew, the strength of the provinces fell from 296 to 229 and that of the princely states from 93 to 70.
4. The Assembly's two functions, constitution-making and ordinary legislation, were performed on the same days.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the Act also made the Assembly a legislative body, the first Parliament of free India. Statement 2 is incorrect: G.V. Mavalankar chaired it as the legislature; Prasad chaired it as the constituent body. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is incorrect: the two tasks were performed on separate days.
w: '4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Constituent Assembly of 1946:

1. It was constituted in November 1946 under the scheme of the Cabinet Mission Plan.
2. The British Indian members were chosen directly by the voters of the provinces, on adult franchise.
3. The Cabinet Mission's scheme for the Assembly more or less satisfied the Muslim League.
4. Population was the yardstick for allotting seats, with about one seat for each five million people.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the British Indian members were indirectly elected and the state members nominated. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is incorrect: the rule was about one seat per million. So only two of the statements are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: statements 1, 3 are correct, so 2 of 4 are correct
'Only one' miscounts: statements 1, 3 are correct, so 2 of 4 are correct
'Only three' miscounts: statements 1, 3 are correct, so 2 of 4 are correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the sittings of the Constituent Assembly:

1. It worked for 2 years, 11 months and 18 days, from December 1946 to November 1949.
2. It held 11 sessions.
3. 114 days were devoted to considering the Draft Constitution.
4. The total expenditure incurred on making the Constitution amounted to Rs 64 lakh.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Assembly worked for 2 years, 11 months and 18 days, from December 1946 to November 1949. Statement 2 is correct: it held 11 sessions. Statement 3 is correct: 114 days were spent on the Draft Constitution. Statement 4 is correct: the total expenditure on making the Constitution was about Rs 64 lakh. So all four of the statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: statements 1, 2, 3, 4 are correct, so 4 of 4 are correct
'Only two' miscounts: statements 1, 2, 3, 4 are correct, so 4 of 4 are correct
'Only three' miscounts: statements 1, 2, 3, 4 are correct, so 4 of 4 are correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Objectives Resolution:

1. It was adopted unanimously on the very day on which Nehru moved it.
2. Depressed classes were among the groups for whom the Resolution assured safeguards, along with minorities.
3. It declared that all power and authority of independent India would be derived from the Constituent Assembly.
4. It was drafted and moved by the Drafting Committee headed by B.R. Ambedkar.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it was moved on 13 December 1946 and adopted on 22 January 1947. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: they were to be derived from the people. Statement 4 is incorrect: Nehru moved it on 13 December 1946, months before the Drafting Committee was set up on 29 August 1947. So only one of the statements is correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: statements 2 are correct, so 1 of 4 are correct
'Only two' miscounts: statements 2 are correct, so 1 of 4 are correct
'Only three' miscounts: statements 2 are correct, so 1 of 4 are correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: On 9 December 1946 the Constituent Assembly began its work with many of its members absent.
Statement-II: The Muslim League stayed away from that meeting because it insisted on a separate state of Pakistan.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: on 9 December 1946 only 207 members attended because the League's members stayed away. Statement-II is correct and is the cause of the thin attendance, so it explains Statement-I.
w: Statement-II is the very reason for the thin attendance, so it does explain Statement-I.
Statement-II is correct: the League boycotted the meeting.
Statement-I is correct: the League members did not attend.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The members of the Constituent Assembly from British India were indirectly elected.
Statement-II: They were elected by the members of the provincial assemblies, who themselves had been elected on adult franchise.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: members from British India were chosen indirectly, the members of each community being elected by that community's members in the provincial assembly. Statement-II is incorrect: the provincial assemblies had themselves been elected on a limited franchise (tax, property and other qualifications), not on adult franchise.
w: Statement-II cannot explain Statement-I because it is itself incorrect: the franchise was limited.
Statement-II is not correct, so the pair cannot both be correct.
Statement-I is correct: election was indirect.

questions.q:
Match the step towards a Constituent Assembly in List-I with the year in which it was taken, given in List-II.

List-I
A. First proposal of the idea of a Constituent Assembly, by the communist leader M.N. Roy
B. Indian National Congress officially demanded the Assembly
C. British Government accepted the demand in principle (August Offer)
D. Cripps proposals carrying the idea of a constitution-making body

List-II
1. 1934
2. 1935
3. 1940
4. 1942
questions.e: Roy 1934; INC official demand 1935; August Offer 1940; Cripps 1942.
w: Interchanges Roy's idea (1934) and the Congress's official demand (1935).
Interchanges the August Offer (1940) and the Cripps proposals (1942).
Pairs the British acceptance with 1934 and Roy with 1940, which reverses the order of events.

concepts.name: Key dates, committees and the drafting process
concepts.description: The calendar of the Assembly, the major and minor committees with their chairmen, the Drafting Committee and the three readings of the draft.
concepts.idea: Committee chairmen, drafting stages and dates are the most swappable facts of this topic.
concepts.rule: Eight major committees were formed: Union Powers, Union Constitution and States (Nehru), Provincial Constitution and the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights etc. (Patel), Steering and Rules of Procedure (Prasad) and Drafting (Ambedkar). The Advisory Committee had sub-committees headed by Kripalani, H.C. Mukherjee, Bardoloi and Thakkar. Rau's draft of October 1947 was reworked by the seven-member Drafting Committee set up on 29 August 1947 (141 days). The first draft went out in February 1948 for about eight months, a revised draft came in October 1948, and the readings ran 4-9 Nov 1948, 15 Nov 1948-17 Oct 1949 (7,653 amendments proposed, 2,473 discussed) and from 14 Nov 1949.
concepts.example: Madhava Rau replaced Mitter, but it was Krishnamachari who replaced Khaitan.

questions.q:
Consider the following events connected with the Constituent Assembly:

A. Creation of the dominions of India and Pakistan
B. Moving of the Objectives Resolution by Jawaharlal Nehru
C. Adoption of the National Flag
D. Election of Dr Rajendra Prasad as President of the Assembly

Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of these events?
questions.e: Prasad elected President 11 Dec 1946; Objectives Resolution 13 Dec 1946; Flag 22 July 1947; dominions 14-15 Aug 1947.
w: Interchanges D and B: Prasad was elected on 11 December 1946, two days before the Resolution was moved on 13 December.
Interchanges C and A: the Flag was adopted on 22 July 1947, before the dominions were created on 14-15 August 1947.
Puts the Flag (22 July 1947) before the Objectives Resolution (13 December 1946), which reverses their order.

questions.q: Under the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas, the Minorities sub-committee was headed by
questions.e: Fundamental Rights - Kripalani; Minorities - H.C. Mukherjee; Assam tribal and excluded areas - Bardoloi; other excluded areas - Thakkar.
w: J.B. Kripalani headed the Fundamental Rights sub-committee.
Gopinath Bardoloi headed the North-East Frontier (Assam) Tribal and Excluded Areas sub-committee.
A.V. Thakkar headed the sub-committee for Excluded and Partially Excluded Areas other than Assam.

questions.q: The Drafting Committee was set up on 29 August 1947 to scrutinise and rework an existing draft of the Constitution. That draft had been produced by the Advisory Branch under
questions.a: Sir B.N. Rau, who held the post of Constitutional Adviser to the Assembly
o: Sir B.N. Rau, who held the post of Constitutional Adviser to the Assembly
H.V.R. Iyengar, who held the post of Secretary to the Assembly
S.N. Mukherjee, who held the post of chief draftsman to the Assembly
Dr B.R. Ambedkar, who held the post of Chairman of the Drafting Committee that later revised the draft
questions.e: The Advisory Branch under B.N. Rau produced the first draft by October 1947; the Drafting Committee was set up on 29 August 1947 to rework it.
w: Iyengar was the Secretary of the Assembly; the Advisory Branch was under Rau.
Mukherjee was the chief draftsman of the Assembly, not head of the Advisory Branch.
Ambedkar chaired the Committee that reworked the draft; he did not head the Advisory Branch.

questions.q: D.P. Khaitan, who died in 1948, was replaced on the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly by
questions.e: N. Madhava Rau replaced B.L. Mitter, who resigned due to ill-health, and T.T. Krishnamachari replaced D.P. Khaitan, who died in 1948.
w: N. Madhava Rau replaced B.L. Mitter, not Khaitan.
Saadullah was among the original members, not a replacement.
Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar was among the original members, not a replacement.

questions.q: During the second reading (clause-by-clause consideration) of the Draft Constitution, the number of amendments proposed and the number actually discussed were respectively
questions.e: 7,653 amendments were proposed and 2,473 were actually discussed and voted upon during the second reading.
w: The number discussed cannot exceed the number proposed.
Transposes digits in both figures (7,635 and 2,437); the correct figures are 7,653 proposed and 2,473 discussed.
Scrambles the digits of both figures (7,356 and 2,743); the correct figures are 7,653 proposed and 2,473 discussed.

List-II

questions.e: Adoption 26 Nov 1949; anthem and song 24 Jan 1950; commencement 26 Jan 1950; elections 25 Oct 1951 to 21 Feb 1952.
w: Interchanges commencement (26 January 1950) and the Anthem (24 January 1950).
Interchanges adoption (26 November 1949) and commencement (26 January 1950).

concepts.name: Enactment, commencement, criticism and sources of the Constitution
concepts.description: Adoption and signing, the Articles in force from 26 November 1949, the date of commencement, repeals, criticism of the Assembly, the borrowed features and the Hindi text.
concepts.idea: Adoption, early commencement of a few Articles and full commencement are three different dates, and each borrowed feature has one source.
concepts.rule: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 with 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules, and members signed on 24 January 1950. Articles 5-9, 60, 324, 366-367, 392 and 393 (with some others) came into force at once; the rest on 26 January 1950, honouring Purna Swaraj Day of 1930. The 1935 and 1947 Acts were repealed, the Privy Council Jurisdiction Act continued. Critics called the Assembly unrepresentative, not sovereign, slow, and dominated by Congress, lawyers and Hindus. Features came from the 1935 Act, Britain, the US, Ireland, Canada, Australia, Weimar Germany, the USSR, France, South Africa and Japan; Article 394A (58th Amendment, 1987) gives the Hindi text.
concepts.example: Procedure established by law comes from Japan; 'due process' is the US model.

questions.q: In a comparison of the time taken by the framers of different constitutions, the framers of which one of the following countries took the longest, about nine years?
questions.e: Australia took about nine years (March 1891 to 9 July 1900). Canada took about 2 years and 6 months, South Africa about one year and the U.S.A. less than four months. The Indian Assembly took 2 years, 11 months and 18 days, which critics called unduly long.
w: Canada took about 2 years and 6 months.
The framers of the U.S. Constitution took less than four months.
South Africa took about one year.

questions.q: The Constitution commenced on 26 January 1950, two months after its adoption. That date was picked because it
questions.a: was the day on which the Congress had observed Purna Swaraj Day in 1930
o: was the day on which the Congress had observed Purna Swaraj Day in 1930
was the day on which the Constituent Assembly had formally adopted the Constitution in 1949
was the day on which the Constituent Assembly had adopted the Objectives Resolution in 1947
was the day on which the Cabinet Mission had announced its plan for India in 1946
questions.e: The date honours 26 January 1930, Purna Swaraj Day, observed after the Lahore Session resolution.
w: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949, two months earlier.
The Objectives Resolution was adopted on 22 January 1947.
The Cabinet Mission published its plan on 16 May 1946.

questions.q: Which one of the following countries' Constitutions served as the model for nominating members to the Rajya Sabha?
questions.e: Irish source - Directive Principles, method of election of the President, nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha.
w: Canada's influence is a strong Centre, residuary powers with the Union and Governors appointed by the Centre.
South Africa is the source of the amendment procedure and the election of Rajya Sabha members.
Australia is the source of the Concurrent List, Article 301 and the joint sitting.
tr: Nomination vs election of Rajya Sabha

questions.q: The provision allowing the suspension of Fundamental Rights during an Emergency is traced to the Constitution of
questions.e: Weimar Constitution - emergency provisions and suspension of Fundamental Rights during an Emergency.
w: The Soviet Constitution is the source of Fundamental Duties and the justice ideals of the Preamble.
Ireland is the source of the Directive Principles, the election of the President and nominations to the Rajya Sabha.
Japan is the source of the phrase 'procedure established by law'.

questions.q: The Constitution as enacted in 1950 had no provision for an authoritative Hindi text. The provision now found in it for this purpose is
questions.a: Article 394A, brought in by the 58th Constitutional Amendment of 1987, in Part XXII
o: Article 394A, brought in by the 58th Constitutional Amendment of 1987, in Part XXII
Article 394, found in the Constitution as originally enacted in 1950, in Part XXII, dealing with the Hindi text
Article 343, found in the Constitution as originally enacted in 1950, in Part XVII
Article 395, brought in by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment of 1976, in Part XXII
questions.e: The 58th Amendment Act, 1987 inserted Article 394A in Part XXII for an authoritative Hindi translation.
w: Article 394 deals with commencement, not with the Hindi text.
Article 343 declares the official language of the Union; it does not provide an authoritative Hindi text of the Constitution.
Article 395 deals with repeals; the Hindi text provision came in 1987, not 1976.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the adoption of the Constitution:

1. On 26 November 1949 Ambedkar moved that the Constitution as settled by the Assembly be passed and it was adopted; the day has been observed as Constitution Day by a Government decision of 19 November 2015.

questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: on 26 November 1949 Ambedkar moved that the Constitution as settled by the Assembly be passed and it was adopted; the day has been observed as Constitution Day by a Government decision of 19 November 2015. Statement 2 is incorrect: at adoption it contained 8 Schedules, not 12. Statement 3 is correct: 284 of the 299 members signed the Constitution. Statement 4 is correct: Jana Gana Mana was adopted as the National Anthem on 24 January 1950.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements about the commencement of the Constitution:

1. Article 392, giving the President power to remove difficulties, came into force on 26 November 1949.
2. Article 393, the short title, came into force on 26 November 1949.

4. Article 394A, on the Hindi text, was in force from 26 November 1949.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 392 was in force from 26 November 1949. Statement 2 is correct: so was Article 393, the short title. Statement 3 is correct: the provisions on citizenship, the provisional Parliament and the like came into force at once, namely Articles 5-9, 60, 324, 366, 367, 379, 380, 388, 391, 392 and 393. Statement 4 is incorrect: Article 394A was inserted only by the 58th Amendment Act, 1987.

3. The Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act, 1949 was repealed under Article 395 on that day.

questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the bulk of the Constitution commenced on 26 January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day. Statement 2 is correct: the Lahore Session of the Congress in December 1929 resolved on Purna Swaraj, and 26 January 1930 was observed as Purna Swaraj Day. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act, 1949 was continued temporarily to complete pending matters, not repealed on that day.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.

4. Critics said it was dominated by the Hindu community.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the objection was that the members were not directly elected by the people; they were indirectly elected, and only the state members were nominated, by their rulers. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is correct.

Consider the following statements about the Constituent Assembly:

questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Assembly was criticised as time-consuming. Statement 2 is correct: it was criticised as dominated by the Congress party. Statement 4 is correct: it was formed under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946 and became a fully sovereign body through the Indian Independence Act, 1947. So only three of the statements are correct.

'Only two' miscounts: statements 1, 2, 4 are correct, so 3 of 4 are correct

w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.

Consider the following statements about the sources of the Indian Constitution:

1. Judicial review is traced to the US Constitution.
2. The vesting of residuary powers in the States is traced to the Canadian Constitution.
3. The words 'equal protection of the laws' in Article 14 are commonly traced to the US Constitution.
4. The phrase 'procedure established by law' in Article 21 is traced to the US Constitution.

questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the Canadian model vests residuary powers in the Centre, and so does the Indian Constitution. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Hindi translation is construed to have the same meaning as the English original and is deemed the authoritative Hindi text. So only one of the statements is correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: statements 1 are correct, so 1 of 4 are correct
'Only two' miscounts: statements 1 are correct, so 1 of 4 are correct
'Only three' miscounts: statements 1 are correct, so 1 of 4 are correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: According to critics, the Constituent Assembly was not a sovereign body.
Statement-II: The critics pointed out that the Assembly was created by the proposals of the British Government and held its sessions with that Government's permission.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: a standing criticism was that the Constituent Assembly was not a sovereign body. Statement-II is correct: critics pointed out that it was created by the proposals of the British Government and held its sessions with that Government's permission; these two points are exactly the critics' ground for the charge, so Statement-II explains Statement-I.
w: Rejected: II does explain I (the critics' charge rests on exactly these two points).
Rejected: Statement-II is correct.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The strength of the Constituent Assembly fell from 389 to 299 after the Partition.
Statement-II: The original 389 seats comprised 292 from the Governors' Provinces, 93 from the princely states and 4 from the Chief Commissioners' Provinces.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: after the Partition the strength fell from 389 to 299. Statement-II is correct: the original 389 seats comprised 292 from the Governors' Provinces, 93 from the princely states and 4 from the Chief Commissioners' Provinces, but the make-up of the original strength does not explain why the strength fell; the fall followed the withdrawal of members from areas that went to Pakistan.
w: Statement-II only describes the original composition; it gives no cause for the fall.
Statement-II is correct: 292 + 93 + 4 = 389.
Statement-I is correct: the strength fell to 299.
